articles.title: We’d rather die than give up land: Siang villagers on proposed dam project
articles.summary: Adi tribals in Arunachal’s Siang oppose the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project as dao seizures by security forces fuel anger and protests.
articles.body: GEKU: Every morning, John Panyang ties a dao around his waist. The two-foot-long machete, carried in a bamboo or wooden sheath and slung across the shoulder, is an everyday companion for the Adi people of Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang region. Farmers use it to clear vegetation, cut bamboo and tend their fields. It is also woven into community life and identity — much like the kirpan is for Sikhs.But in villages at the centre of a growing resistance to the proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), it has become a source of tension.Security forces have reportedly seized the traditional implement from villagers in Riga and Pangkang, across Siang river from Geku, following an alleged attack on personnel with a dao. The seizures, carried out as part of heightened security measures against anti-dam protests, have stirred anger in the Adi community. Many Adi farmers openly defied the order to tend to their fields, especially in Geku — the nerve centre of protest against SUMP.The main reservoir of the proposed mega dam is reportedly planned near Geku village, about 35 km downstream from district headquarters Yingkiong.“We tie the dao around our waist before stepping out of our homes every morning. It is an essential part of our lives. Why should we be stopped from carrying it to our fields?” said Panyang, a farmer living along Siang river in Geku town.Residents fear the govt’s security offensive is aimed at silencing opposition to the proposed dam and the pre-feasibility survey. Govt sources said NHPC wants to undertake drilling as part of the process of preparing the project’s pre-feasibility report. However, villagers have opposed any drilling in the riverbed, insisting that they do not want a feasibility report on the project.“We will not abandon our settlement. We would rather die here than surrender our land. If the Chinese dam is the threat, why should our govt build another mega dam in the Siang belt, nearly 300 km from the Line of Actual Control? The govt should explore alternatives closer to the border to counter China’s plans,” Panyang said.Twenty-seven villages across Upper Siang and Siang districts have joined hands to resist the project. The protests, however, have begun to affect the agricultural cycle, with several farmers unable to tend their paddy fields regularly because of demonstrations and meetings to plan further resistance.Along Siang river and its adjoining slopes in the narrow strips between hills, villagers cultivate traditional rice varieties such as ‘Gegong’, ‘Itanagar’, ‘Ngotsum’ and ‘Taker’. The latter is particularly significant among the Adis, who use it to prepare traditional rice beer.The agitation has also affected community festivities. On Sept 1, the Adi community in Geku curtailed its biggest festival, Solung, limiting celebrations to flag-hoisting at Gidii Notko, the traditional festival ground. The festival is usually celebrated over three to four days.For nearly 1,000 families in Geku, the proposed dam represents a threat to their homes, farmland and ancestral ties. Residents fear that construction upstream or downstream could expose the township to submergence risks arising from water storage or release.Most families in the remote settlement depend on agriculture, with only around 10 to 15 govt employees among its nearly 1,000 households. Many Adi families have lived on community land in the area for generations. In the 1960s, they moved from their original settlement at Kumku, situated on a hilltop about six kilometres away, to the riverbank to cultivate rice, oranges and vegetables.“We do not want compensation in exchange for losing our homeland. Where will we go, and what will we eat?” asked Oken Boli Panggyeng, a homemaker. “No dam survey, no detailed project report. That is our slogan,” she said, adding that villagers were prepared to prioritise the agitation over the upcoming paddy harvest.“Harvesting will begin in the first week of Nov. We may lose our paddy, but we do not want to lose our land. articles.title: Londonderry: Explosive device sent to hotel
articles.summary: Police condemn the "reckless and targeted attack" after the explosive was sent to a Londonderry hotel.
articles.body:
A suspicious package delivered to a hotel in Londonderry contained a "viable" explosive device, police have said.

Army bomb experts were sent to the hotel at Ebrington Square in the city's Waterside after the package was discovered at about 15:20 GMT on Tuesday.

They carried out a controlled explosion on the device, which was later taken away for a forensic examination.

Det Supt Kearney of the Police Service of Northern Ireland said: "I condemn this reckless and targeted attack."

The detective said that "a number of people" were evacuated from the hotel, along with staff from neighbouring premises.

A Halloween funfair had been taking place a short distance away from the hotel.

It remained open during the security alert.

Justice Minister Naomi Long condemned the incident, calling it "abhorrent".

"The viable device was placed in the vicinity of families and young people celebrating Halloween, Long said.

"It was an utterly shameful and dangerous act and the people behind it have shown absolutely no regard to the community or businesses affected," she added.

She paid tribute to the police officers who responded to the incident, "once again putting themselves in harm's way to ensure the safety of the public".

SDLP MLA Mark H Durkan told BBC Radio Foyle's North West Today programme police officers acted swiftly and that his thoughts were with them, the hotel staff and the hotel guests who were impacted.

"This is extremely traumatic for staff and those staying at the hotel," Durkan said.

"This should be a positive week for Derry, with all the events going on with Halloween in the city, there is a lot of buzz, but this has certainly painted a less positive picture of this city.

"This is not representative of Derry and the vast majority of people in this city, who would, like me, completely reject this."

Julie Middleton, Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) assembly member for Foyle, told BBC Radio Ulster's Good Morning Ulster programme on Wednesday that she was "deeply disturbed and disgusted".

"There is no excuse to leave a viable device anywhere at all, but in the middle of Ebrington Square, where you have people at their work, families out enjoying some half-term fun and tourists visiting and unfortunately this was designed to cause disruption and with any viable device, it was obviously designed to cause harm."

Middleton said many children would also be in the vicinity enjoying the fun fair.

"To think anyone would place something like this near our children, or anyone for that matter, is just deeply wrong."

articles.title: Myanmar national bound down for hosting 28 foreigners in Delhi without mandatory reporting
articles.summary: Delhi Police bound down a Myanmar UNHCR cardholder for allegedly hosting 28 foreigners in Uttam Nagar without filing mandatory Form C, FRRO says.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has bound down a Myanmar national holding a UNHCR (Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) card for allegedly accommodating 28 foreign nationals at a guest house in Uttam Nagar over a period of time without submitting mandatory details to authorities.According to police, the man allegedly hosted 23 US nationals and five Norwegian nationals at the premises but failed to file Form C (earlier referred to as Form III), which is required to be submitted by those providing accommodation to foreign nationals.The case was registered at Dabri police station on Oct 23 following a complaint from Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO).Police said the Myanmar national, who lives with his family in a four-room apartment in Chanakya Place, Uttam Nagar, allegedly used two rooms of the flat as a guest house and rented them out to foreign nationals over a period of time.The complaint, forwarded to DCP (Dwarka), alleged that the mandatory details of foreign guests were not submitted as required under immigration rules.FRRO termed the alleged lapse a violation of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, and sought action under Sections 8 and 23 of the Act, Section 17 of the Immigration and Foreigners Rules, 2025, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Following the complaint, Dabri police registered an FIR under Sections 8 and 23 of the Act and launched an investigation.Police said he has been bound down, requiring the Myanmar national to join the investigation whenever called and inform authorities before leaving the city.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Enem 2026 Matemática: Veja vídeos de até 1 min com dicas para a prova | G1
articles.standfirst: Professor piauiense explica, em vídeos curtos, conceitos de média, mediana, escala e função do 2º grau, conteúdos frequentes no exame.
articles.summary: Professor piauiense explica, em vídeos curtos, conceitos de média, mediana, escala e função do 2º grau, conteúdos frequentes no exame.
articles.body:
Com a aproximação do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026, o g1 preparou uma série de vídeos com dicas de professores sobre conteúdos que costumam ser cobrados na prova. Os especialistas explicam conceitos, destacam erros frequentes e orientam os candidatos na reta final de estudos.

O material integra o projeto Ingresso Universitário , página especial do g1 voltada a candidatos que buscam uma vaga no ensino superior. As provas do Enem 2026 serão aplicadas nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro.

O professor de Matemática Alexandre Kessler revisa os conceitos de média, moda e mediana e destaca os principais cuidados ao resolver questões sobre medidas estatísticas.

No vídeo, o professor dá atenção especial à mediana. A orientação é organizar os dados em ordem crescente e verificar a quantidade de elementos antes de realizar os cálculos.

Outro tema destacado por Alexandre Kessler é a escala , que representa a relação entre a medida de um desenho e seu tamanho real. Segundo o professor, as questões sobre o assunto têm ficado mais complexas nos últimos anos.

Ele explica que o Enem também passou a cobrar o conceito em questões envolvendo área e volume. Nesses casos, os candidatos precisam adaptar os cálculos, utilizando a raiz quadrada para áreas e a raiz cúbica para volumes.

Para finalizar, Alexandre Kessler destaca as funções do segundo grau . No vídeo, ele explica como identificar questões que envolvem valores máximos e mínimos e aponta os conceitos que merecem mais atenção durante a resolução.

O professor também apresenta dicas práticas para interpretar os enunciados e evitar erros comuns. Segundo ele, compreender o que a questão pede é fundamental para escolher a estratégia correta de resolução.

articles.title: TikTok bane conta que transmitiu ao vivo agressão que matou engenheiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha, de 30 anos, morreu após ser abordado por ao menos sete suspeitos, que gravaram o crime e já foram identificados pela Polícia Civil. Dois deles, de 14 e 17 anos, foram apreendidos.
articles.summary: O TikTok baniu a conta que transmitiu agressão ao engenheiro Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha em Santos; polícia já identificou sete envolvidos no crime investigado como latrocínio.
articles.body:
A conta usada pelo grupo que agrediu e roubou o engenheiro ambiental e mestrando Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha, de 30 anos , foi banida pelo TikTok. Os suspeitos fizeram uma transmissão ao vivo durante o crime que resultou na morte cerebral da vítima em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo.

Marcelo participava de uma apresentação da Banda Esquerdantina, em apoio à reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), na madrugada de sábado (24). Ele se afastou do evento para ir ao banheiro, quando foi abordado e agredido por ao menos sete suspeitos , que gravaram o crime.

Por meio de nota, a plataforma de vídeos confirmou ao g1 que a conta foi banida por violar as Diretrizes de Comunidade . A rede social acrescentou que está colaborando com as autoridades policiais nas investigações do caso.

"Lamentamos profundamente o ocorrido com Marcelo e nos solidarizamos com a sua família. A segurança é uma prioridade máxima para o TikTok e mantemos uma postura de tolerância zero contra qualquer forma de comportamento violento e criminoso em nossa plataforma", destacou.

Grupo fez live agredindo e roubando engenheiro que se afastou de ato pró-Lula em Santos, SP — Foto: Reprodução

O g1 consultou as Diretrizes da Comunidade, que se aplicam a todos os usuários e definem as regras do que é e o que não é permitido no TikTok. Entre elas, estão:

Comportamento violento e criminoso: É proibido conteúdo que envolva ameaças, incentivo ou exaltação de atos violentos, promoção de crimes ou orientações sobre como cometer práticas prejudiciais.

Comportamento e discurso de ódio: É proibido conteúdo que promova o ódio ou ataque pessoas com base em atributos protegidos, como raça, religião, gênero ou orientação sexual.

Organizações e pessoas violentas e odiosas: São proibidas pessoas ou grupos que promovam violência ou disseminem ódio, incluindo extremistas violentos, organizações criminosas ou aqueles responsáveis por violência em larga escala. Também é proibido apoiar, recrutar ou promover essas entidades.

A plataforma não especificou quais foram as regras aplicadas neste caso. O g1 questionou se a mulher que participava da transmissão ao vivo, dividindo a tela com os suspeitos, e os telespectadores também tiveram a conta banida, mas ainda não obteve resposta.

Dois adolescentes foram apreendidos na terça-feira (27) , suspeitos de integrar o grupo. Conforme apurado pela TV Tribuna, afiliada da Globo, um jovem de 17 anos é lutador de boxe e considerado suspeito de ter dado um soco que fez a vítima cair no chão.

O outro menor tem 14 anos e se apresentou no 3º Distrito Policial (DP), onde foi ouvido e apreendido. Além dos dois adolescentes, a equipe do 4º DP identificou outros cinco suspeitos, sendo três menores e dois maiores. Os mandados de prisão e internação provisória já foram expedidos.

De acordo com a Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP), o caso é investigado como latrocínio porque o celular e outros pertences de Marcelo foram levados pelos agressores.

Ainda de acordo com a SSP-SP, a equipe do 4º DP está empenhada em localizar os agressores da vítima. Os investigadores também trabalham a partir de depoimentos de testemunhas para individualizar a conduta de cada agressor.

Questionada pela equipe de reportagem, a SSP-SP não informou se apura a possibilidade de crimes de ódio.

Segundo testemunhas ouvidas pelo g1 , os amigos estranharam a demora de Marcelo no banheiro e começaram a procurá-lo. Ainda de acordo com os relatos, o engenheiro foi encontrado desacordado na esquina da Avenida Conselheiro Nébias com a Rua Henrique Ablas.

O jovem chegou a ser socorrido pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e internado na Santa Casa de Santos. Ele teve a morte cerebral confirmada na segunda-feira (26) , após ser transferido para o Hospital São Paulo, da Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp).

Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha foi agredido após se afastar de um ato político pró-Lula em Santos — Foto: Redes sociais

Por meio de nota, a Esquerdantina confirmou ao g1 que Marcelo foi agredido e deixado inconsciente no local, onde foi socorrido. O grupo afirmou que exige "a rápida apuração e consequente punição aos responsáveis".

Embora a motivação da agressão ainda não tenha sido esclarecida, a Esquerdantina também manifestou repúdio à homofobia.

"Manifestamos nossa solidariedade à vítima e seus familiares, bem como nosso firme repúdio à homofobia, alertando para os riscos que todos corremos ao naturalizar, proteger ou promover o ódio como método de intimidação política", ressaltou.

articles.title: Pesquisa abre caminhos para tratamentos de doenças hereditárias | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo publicado na revista científica Nature contou com participação de pesquisadoras brasileiras da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de São Paulo (FMUSP). Análise identificou o papel da proteína BACH2 na regulação da chamada hemoglobina fetal.
articles.summary: Estudo publicado na revista científica Nature contou com participação de pesquisadoras brasileiras da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de São Paulo (FMUSP).
articles.body:
Glóbulos vermelhos do sangue. — Foto: Pixabay

Uma pesquisa com dados genéticos de mais de 28 mil pessoas identificou um mecanismo que pode abrir novos caminhos para o tratamento de doenças hereditárias do sangue , como a anemia falciforme e a beta-talassemia.

➡️O estudo, publicado na revista científica Nature e que contou com participação de pesquisadoras brasileiras da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de São Paulo (FMUSP), identificou o papel da proteína BACH2 na regulação da chamada hemoglobina fetal , uma forma de hemoglobina que predomina durante a gestação.

Segundo os pesquisadores, a proteína atua como um "freio" da produção de hemoglobina fetal. Ao reduzir a ação desse freio em células cultivadas no laboratório, os cientistas conseguiram aumentar a produção de hemoglobina fetal.

Ester Sabino, imunologista e titular do Departamento de Patologia da Faculdade de Medicina da USP, explica que já se sabia há muito tempo que, aqueles que possuem níveis altos de hemoglobina fetal durante a vida uterina, tendem a ter uma melhora no quadro de anemia falciforme .

Assim, o aumento promovido a partir da descoberta da atuação da proteína pode ajudar a amenizar os efeitos de doenças hereditárias do sangue .

"Cada vez que você descobre um caminho pelo qual uma proteína é produzida, facilita encontrar caminhos de tratar os pacientes", analisa Sabino.

A descoberta amplia o conhecimento sobre os mecanismos que controlam a produção dessa proteína e aponta um possível caminho para desenvolver novas estratégias terapêuticas.

🩸A hemoglobina é a proteína presente nos glóbulos vermelhos responsável pelo transporte de oxigênio pelo organismo . Durante o desenvolvimento humano, a hemoglobina fetal é gradualmente substituída pela forma predominante na vida adulta.

Em pessoas com anemia falciforme, uma alteração genética faz com que a hemoglobina adulta tenha um funcionamento anormal, levando à deformação dos glóbulos vermelhos.

Já a beta-talassemia é uma doença hereditária caracterizada pela produção reduzida ou ausente de uma das partes da hemoglobina adulta.

Os pesquisadores explicam que, nesses contextos, aumentar a produção de hemoglobina fetal é uma estratégia de interesse para o tratamento.

E o estudo investigou justamente os mecanismos genéticos envolvidos na regulação dessa produção e identificou a BACH2 como um dos fatores que a restringem.

Segundo o grupo, uma variante genética associada a níveis mais elevados de hemoglobina fetal reduz a expressão de BACH2. Nos experimentos realizados em laboratório, a redução ou inibição dessa proteína também aumentou a expressão da hemoglobina fetal.

Os resultados indicaram ainda que a BACH2 restringe a ativação promovida pela NRF2. Essa relação entre as duas proteínas constitui um mecanismo de regulação que pode ser explorado em pesquisas futuras.

Análise genética reuniu dados de mais de 28 mil pessoas

Para investigar os fatores genéticos associados à produção de hemoglobina fetal, os pesquisadores realizaram uma análise que reuniu 28.279 pessoas de diferentes ancestralidades.

O estudo identificou 91 associações genéticas independentes distribuídas por 12 regiões do genoma. Em uma dessas regiões, os pesquisadores encontraram uma variante associada a níveis mais elevados de hemoglobina fetal e à redução da expressão de BACH2.

"Em estudos genéticos, para que se chegue a descobertas, é necessário um grande número de pessoas, de populações de lugares diferentes", analisa Sabino.

A partir dessa pista genética, a equipe realizou experimentos para investigar se a proteína tinha um papel direto na regulação da hemoglobina fetal. Os resultados reforçaram a relação identificada na análise genética e ajudaram a esclarecer o mecanismo biológico envolvido.

A combinação de dados genéticos de pessoas e experimentos funcionais foi importante para relacionar a variante identificada à atuação de BACH2 na produção da hemoglobina fetal.

Combinação de estratégias apresentou resultado promissor

O estudo também investigou a relação entre BACH2 e BCL11A, outro regulador conhecido da produção de hemoglobina fetal e alvo de estratégias terapêuticas.

Os experimentos indicaram que as duas proteínas atuam por mecanismos independentes. Quando os pesquisadores reduziram a ação de BACH2 e de BCL11A simultaneamente, observaram um aumento da hemoglobina fetal superior ao obtido com a redução de cada uma das proteínas isoladamente.

O resultado sugere que atuar sobre diferentes mecanismos de regulação pode ser uma possibilidade para pesquisas voltadas ao aumento da hemoglobina fetal.

Apesar de promissora, a descoberta ainda precisa avançar antes que essa abordagem possa ser considerada uma alternativa de tratamento. Segundo os pesquisadores, os experimentos não demonstram, por si só, que a estratégia seja segura ou eficaz em pacientes.

"Esse é só o primeiro passo. Depois que a gente entende esses mecanismos, é preciso testar inicialmente em modelos animais e, depois, realizar estudos em humanos para só então desenvolver um tratamento seguro", finaliza Ester Sabino.

articles.title: Eleição nos EUA: apuração em tempo real mostrará se Trump terá maioria | G1
articles.standfirst: Página especial do g1 vai mostrar como está a disputa para a Câmara, o Senado e governo estaduais norte-americanos. Midterms estão marcadas para 3 de novembro.
articles.summary: Página especial do g1 vai mostrar como está a disputa para a Câmara, o Senado e governo estaduais norte-americanos. Midterms estão marcadas para 3 de novembro.
articles.body:
Os americanos vão às urnas na príxima terça-feira (3) para as eleições de meio de mandato, as midterms . O g1 preparou uma página especial para que o leitor possa acompanhar a cobertura da disputa e a apuração dos votos em tempo real.

▶️ Contexto: Diferentemente do Brasil, o Congresso dos Estados Unidos é renovado parcialmente a cada dois anos. Quando ocorrem na metade do mandato presidencial, essas eleições são chamadas de midterms.

Os deputados norte-americanos têm mandatos de dois anos, enquanto os senadores, de seis.

Com isso, a cada dois anos, o país renova toda a Câmara dos Representantes e cerca de um terço do Senado.

Sendo assim, em novembro, estarão em disputa todas as 435 cadeiras da Câmara e 35 das 100 do Senado.

No g1 , uma página especial terá mapas que vão mostrar como está a apuração em todo o país para a Câmara, Senado e governo estadual. Também será possível detalhar como está a disputa em cada estado.

Mapa de página especial do g1 mostra a apuração das midterms nos EUA — Foto: Reprodução

Para saber, por exemplo, quem são os candidatos que disputam as eleições no Texas, basta clicar no estado. A ferramenta vai mostrar o desempenho de cada concorrente e o avanço da contagem dos votos por condado.

Mapa mostra exemplo da apuração para o Senado no Texas — Foto: Reprodução

A ferramenta também vai mostrar quantas cadeiras cada partido ainda precisa conquistar para alcançar a maioria na Câmara ou no Senado. À medida que os resultados forem sendo divulgados, uma barra vai mostrar como está o placar de cada partido.

Um partido precisa eleger mais de 50 senadores para ter maioria no Senado.

A legenda que eleger 218 deputados ou mais terá o controle da Câmara.

Trabalhadores eleitorais participam do processo de contagem de votos para a eleição presidencial dos EUA de 2024 no dia da eleição — Foto: Patrick T. Fallon / AFP

Os Estados Unidos não têm um órgão que centralize a apuração, como o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) no Brasil. Cada estado tem autonomia para organizar as eleições, e os procedimentos de votação e contagem dos votos podem variar pelo país.

Em alguns estados e condados, a votação é feita em cédulas de papel, enquanto outros utilizam urnas eletrônicas. Também é possível votar pelo correio.

Diante dessa complexidade, a apuração dos votos nos Estados Unidos pode levar dias, já que cada estado faz a própria contagem. Ou seja, o público pode ter que esperar até depois de 3 de novembro para saber qual partido terá maioria na Câmara e no Senado.

Nesse cenário, o papel da imprensa é fundamental. A projeção de vencedores antes da contagem oficial é feita por veículos de imprensa — o g1 e a Globo, como a maioria das redes internacionais, adotam os dados da Associated Press (AP).

Há 180 anos, a AP atua na cobertura e na apuração dos resultados das eleições americanas. A agência conta com cerca de 4.000 repórteres espalhados pelos distritos eleitorais e escritórios eleitorais dos condados do país para checar dados.

As informações são coletadas de forma padronizada e analisadas com base em uma série de fatores, o que permite que a agência anuncie vencedores com segurança.

A AP não faz diretamente a contagem manual dos votos depositados nas urnas. Esse trabalho é realizado pelas autoridades eleitorais locais responsáveis pela administração das eleições em cada estado americano.

Além disso, a Associated Press pode declarar um vencedor em determinado estado antes mesmo de 100% dos votos serem contados.

articles.title: Câncer em situações de crise: como preparar o SUS para garantir a continuidade do cuidado à população? | G1
articles.standfirst: Pandemias, inundações e desigualdades sociais expõem fragilidades da assistência oncológica no Brasil e reforçam a necessidade de integrar a resiliência às políticas públicas de saúde
articles.summary: Pandemias, inundações e desigualdades sociais expõem fragilidades da assistência oncológica no Brasil e reforçam a necessidade de integrar a resiliência às políticas públicas de saúde
articles.body:
Câncer em situações de crise: como preparar o SUS para garantir a continuidade do cuidado à população? — Foto: Wikipedia

O que acontece com uma pessoa com câncer quando uma pandemia interrompe ou adia consultas; ou inundações comprometem hospitais e restringem o acesso aos serviços de saúde?

Para quem depende de diagnóstico oportuno, tratamento contínuo e acompanhamento especializado, a interrupção ou o adiamento da assistência pode ter consequências graves.

Em oncologia, manter o cuidado durante uma emergência não é apenas uma questão de organização dos serviços. É uma prioridade para proteger e salvar vidas e reduzir as desigualdades.

No Brasil, esse desafio ganha dimensão diante da crescente carga da doença. O câncer é a segunda principal causa de morte no país . E as projeções da Agência Internacional de Pesquisa em Câncer (IARC) indicam que o número anual de casos poderá aumentar 84% entre 2022 e 2050.

Esse cenário exige não apenas ampliar a capacidade de prevenção, diagnóstico e tratamento, mas também preparar o sistema de saúde. O sistema precisa continuar funcionando diante de crises cada vez mais frequentes e interconectadas.

Nesse sentido, exemplos significativos como a pandemia de Covid-19 e as inundações que atingiram o Rio Grande do Sul em 2024 demonstraram como emergências de naturezas distintas podem comprometer a continuidade da assistência à saúde da população.

Nessas situações de crise, consultas e procedimentos podem ser adiados. Unidades de saúde podem perder sua capacidade operacional e pacientes podem enfrentar dificuldades de deslocamento, além, é claro, da dificuldade de acesso a medicamentos e acompanhamento clínico. Os efeitos tendem a ser mais intensos entre pessoas que já enfrentam barreiras econômicas, territoriais e sociais.

Resiliência é manter o cuidado, não apenas responder à emergência

A experiência brasileira evidencia uma questão fundamental: a preparação para crises precisa incluir explicitamente o controle do câncer. Embora o SUS garanta acesso universal e gratuito, persistem desafios relacionados ao financiamento, às desigualdades regionais e à coordenação entre os serviços.

Resiliência significa a capacidade de antecipar ameaças, absorver impactos, adaptar a organização dos serviços e aprender com as estratégias de mitigação adotadas. Além disso, é preciso recuperar suas funções sem comprometer o acesso da população. Portanto, não se trata apenas de restabelecer o funcionamento dos hospitais depois de uma emergência, mas de preservar as etapas essenciais da jornada oncológica, da prevenção e do diagnóstico aos cuidados paliativos.

Essa perspectiva foi debatida em um workshop nacional realizado no Rio de Janeiro, em dezembro de 2025. O evento foi organizado pela IARC, pela Organização Pan-Americana da Saúde (Opas) e pelo Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA).

O encontro reuniu especialistas de diferentes setores: formuladores de políticas públicas, profissionais de saúde, pesquisadores e representantes da sociedade civil. O objetivo foi identificar prioridades de ação, considerando as experiências da pandemia de Covid-19 e das inundações no Rio Grande do Sul.

As discussões resultaram em artigo cientifico, publicado no periódico The Lancet Regional Health – Americas .

No artigo, apontamos que fortalecer a resiliência exige intervenções articuladas em quatro dimensões: governança, prestação de serviços, recursos e financiamento.

Essas áreas não funcionam isoladamente. A falta de informação confiável, por exemplo, dificulta a identificação de pacientes que tiveram o tratamento interrompido.

Sem coordenação entre os gestores, torna-se mais difícil encaminhá-los a outros serviços. E, sem recursos financeiros disponíveis, a resposta pode não chegar a tempo.

Cinco prioridades para fortalecer o controle do câncer no Brasil e no SUS

A primeira prioridade é incorporar a assistência oncológica aos planos de preparação e resposta a emergências.

Planos de contingência devem definir quais serviços precisam permanecer operacionais, como reorganizar os fluxos assistenciais e como garantir a continuidade dos tratamentos essenciais.

A pactuação entre União, estados e municípios é indispensável para que as medidas sejam executáveis em diferentes territórios.

A segunda é fortalecer e integrar os sistemas de informação em saúde, hoje fragmentados . Dados interoperáveis ajudam a identificar pacientes com consultas, exames ou tratamentos pendentes, acompanhar interrupções e redistribuir a demanda entre unidades. Além disso, é preciso assegurar que gestores e profissionais tenham acesso às informações necessárias à tomada de decisão e que a proteção dos dados pessoais seja garantida.

A terceira prioridade é proteger a infraestrutura e a força de trabalho. Hospitais, serviços de radioterapia, laboratórios, redes de transporte e sistemas de abastecimento precisam ser considerados nos planos de contingência.

Também é necessário preparar os profissionais para atuar em condições excepcionais. Condições que forneçam protocolos claros, equipes de apoio e mecanismos de comunicação que facilitem a reorganização da assistência.

A quarta é planejar a recuperação da assistência com foco na equidade. Retomar os atendimentos por ordem de capacidade operacional, sem considerar as necessidades clínicas e sociais, pode ampliar desigualdades preexistentes.

Pessoas com maior risco clínico, tratamentos interrompidos e dificuldades de acesso precisam ser identificadas e priorizadas, com apoio da atenção primária em saúde.

Por fim, é necessário garantir mecanismos de financiamento flexíveis para situações de emergência. A capacidade de mobilizar recursos rapidamente, recompor estruturas danificadas e ampliar temporariamente a oferta de serviços pode determinar a velocidade da recuperação.

A previsibilidade do financiamento e a definição prévia de responsabilidades também ajudam a evitar que a resposta dependa exclusivamente de medidas improvisadas.

Essas prioridades não exigem necessariamente a criação de uma estrutura paralela ao SUS. Ao contrário, apontam para a necessidade de fortalecer mecanismos existentes, melhorar a coordenação regional e integrar a resiliência ao planejamento regular da saúde.

A experiência acumulada na atenção primária, nas redes de atenção e nas políticas nacionais de controle do câncer oferece uma base importante para avanço.

A implementação, contudo, depende de compromissos concretos. Responsabilidades institucionais definidas, recursos adequados, indicadores de continuidade assistencial e mecanismos de avaliação capazes de transformar as lições de cada crise em melhorias permanentes.

A participação de pacientes e organizações da sociedade civil é essencial para identificar barreiras que indicadores administrativos nem sempre revelam.

Diante da perspectiva de crescimento dos números do câncer e da ocorrência de crises simultâneas, a questão já não é apenas como ampliar a assistência em condições normais, mas como impedir que emergências interrompam acesso ao diagnóstico e ao tratamento oncológico.

Fortalecer a resiliência do controle do câncer significa reconhecer que a continuidade do cuidado deve ser planejada antes da crise, protegida durante a emergência e aprimorada na recuperação.

Assim, acreditamos que essa é uma oportunidade de reafirmar o compromisso do SUS com a universalidade e a equidade.

Um sistema preparado para enfrentar crises não apenas responde melhor às emergências: também amplia sua capacidade de oferecer cuidado oportuno, coordenado e digno à população.

João Paulo de Biaso Viola é coordenador de Pesquisa e Inovação e vice-Diretor Geral do Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA). Ele recebe financiamento do CNPq e FAPERJ.

Alessandro Jatobá é pesquisador e, atualmente, Vice-presidente Adjunto de Pesquisa e Coleções Biológicas da Fundação Oswaldo Cruz (Fiocruz). Ele recebe financiamento do Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico (CNPq).

Heloise Fernandes Agreli é pesquisadora da International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC). Ela já recebeu financiamento do CNPq.

Beatriz Jardim é epidemiologista e cientista da International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC).

Rafael José Vargas Alves é vice-reitor da Universidade Federal de Ciências da Saúde de Porto Alegre (UFCSPA) e Doutor em Epidemiologia pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS).

Beatriz Jardim e Rafael José Vargas Alves não prestam consultoria, trabalham, possuem ações ou recebem financiamento de qualquer empresa ou organização que poderiam se beneficiar com a publicação deste artigo e não revelaram nenhum vínculo relevante além de seus cargos acadêmicos.

articles.title: El Salvador rushes some 1,000 troops to Haiti after gang ambush, source says
articles.summary: Oct 27 (Reuters) - El Salvador has sent about 1,000 troops to Haiti after four Salvadoran members of a UN-backed security mission went missing in a gang ambu...
articles.body:
Oct 27 (Reuters) - El Salvador has sent about 1,000 troops to Haiti after four Salvadoran members of a UN-backed security mission went missing in a gang ambush on the outskirts of the capital on October 18, a security official in Haiti told Reuters ‌on Tuesday.

The troops' arrival aboard flights in recent days dramatically expands the Central American nation's role in Haiti's long-standing gang conflict. Yet it remains ‌unclear who will command the new Salvadoran contingent, how long it will stay in Haiti or whether more forces will follow.

Neither the Haitian nor Salvadoran government immediately responded to requests for comment. The ​official in Haiti spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the security situation.

The deployment comes as the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force has reached about 2,000 personnel, just over a third of its planned strength a year into its mandate, with little improvement in Haiti's security.

Armed gangs in Haiti have meanwhile expanded their influence over the capital and surrounding regions through extortion and brutal attacks that have displaced nearly 1.5 million people.

Haiti's leaders have sought international security support since 2022, despite the country's fraught ‌history of foreign intervention. Gangs' influence grew rapidly after ⁠the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise, deepening an insecurity crisis that has caused authorities to repeatedly delay elections.

Pierre Esperance, head of Haiti's National Human Rights Defense Network, welcomed the unusually rapid Salvadoran deployment and said he hoped it would help stop ⁠gangs from terrorizing civilians. But he warned that any operation must avoid harming residents trapped in gang-held neighborhoods.

"Not everybody living in gang-controlled areas are gangsters," he said.

President Nayib Bukele last week announced a military operation to recover the missing Salvadorans, who remain unaccounted for since jumping from a burning vehicle during the ambush. He has not said how many troops ​would ​be sent.

The US provided C-130 transport aircraft to help move Salvadoran troops to Haiti, a ​US military official said.

Additional commercial and military flights between San Salvador ‌and Port-au-Prince were visible on flight-tracking site Flightradar24 and were also reported by the Miami Herald.

A photo posted on X on Tuesday by a lawmaker from Bukele's ruling party showed a plane carrying uniformed soldiers, some taking selfies.

Bukele has built strong domestic support through a hardline anti-crime campaign that several right-wing governments in the Americas have sought to emulate. Human rights groups however warn that the crackdown has come at the cost of due process and has been linked to hundreds of deaths in custody.

Bukele said the missing Salvadorans were air force technicians, returning to base from a market, and that he believed they were being ‌held hostage by criminal groups.

No Haitian gang has claimed responsibility for the ambush. Wilson Joseph, ​leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, has released videos denying that his group is holding the ​Salvadorans or was involved in the attack.

Before the ambush, El Salvador had ​deployed at least 124 personnel to the force. Bukele said they were pilots and technicians sent to evacuate wounded personnel, not ‌combatants.

Alongside the international mission, Haiti's government has also hired a private ​military company run by Blackwater founder Erik ​Prince - an ally of US President Donald Trump - which has since 2025 carried out controversial anti-gang drone operations.

Luis Contreras, a Salvadoran security and organized crime analyst, said he expected that at least some of the new troops would operate outside the UN-backed mission's chain of command and could coordinate ​with Prince's firm.

"The UN has lacked the political will to ‌resolve the issue of the gangs in Haiti," he said. "Once the whereabouts of the four members have been established, they will have to ​assess whether to engage in a direct and protracted confrontation."

(Reporting by Sarah Morland in Mexico City, Gerardo Arbaiza in San Salvador and ​Harold Isaac in Port-au-Prince; Editing by Daina Beth Solomon, Bill Berkrot and Jonathan Spicer )

articles.title: Israeli exit polls suggest no clear winner in pivotal general election
articles.summary: Two polls project that veteran PM Benjamin Netanyahu and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot are tied, with neither winning a majority.
articles.body:
Exit polls suggest there is no clear winner of Israel's pivotal general election, with neither veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor former military chief Gadi Eisenkot on track to secure a majority.

Two Israeli broadcasters projected that Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his "Change Bloc" would win 51 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, as would Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies. A third broadcaster's poll gave Netanyahu a lead of three seats.

Much will depend on the role played by the two Arab parties, which were projected to win a record 18 or 19 seats.

Voter turnout on Tuesday was the highest in decades.

It stood at 77.7% when polls closed at 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT), which was the highest at that hour since 1999, the Central Elections Committee said.

Official results will start to be published overnight, but an estimated 600,000 absentee ballots cast mostly by military personnel - around 10% of the total number of votes - will not be fully counted until Thursday.

Once the final results are confirmed, and following consultations with all the political factions, Israel's president will invite the party leader whom he believes has the best chance of success to form a governing coalition - a process that could take weeks.

If they fail, then ultimately there would have to be another election.

At the headquarters of Eisenkot's Yashar party in Tel Aviv, his supporters cheered and chanted "Bibi, go home!" after the initial exit polls published by public broadcaster Kan, Channel 12 and Channel 13 projected that his bloc would emerge as the biggest in the Knesset, with between 52 and 53 seats, compared to 50 seats for Netanyahu's governing coalition.

Eisenkot said they had "made history" and promised to "ensure that the people's decision is translated into a Zionist government: stable and good for all of Israel's citizens".

His ally in the Beyachad party, former prime minister Yair Lapid, said Netanyahu's bloc had suffered a "crushing defeat".

However, there was no sign of surrender at the Jerusalem headquarters of Netanyahu's Likud party, which was projected to be the largest party in parliament.

Supporters there told the BBC that they were nervous. "It's not over until it's over, but I'm sweating," Itzik said.

Netanyahu's ally, Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, said celebrations on the left were "premature", while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir told supporters of his far-right Jewish Power party to pray that the final results would lead to a "full-on right-wing government".

In the early hours of Wednesday, the broadcasters updated their exit polls. Kan and Channel 13's projections showed the blocs tied on 51 seats, while Channel 12 gave Netanyahu's bloc 52 seats and Eisenkot's 49.

Later, Netanyahu appeared at Likud's headquarters and declared in a speech that his right-wing bloc had a "great majority". He also called for the formation of "a strong, right-wing national government".

The two Arab parties - the United Arab List and the Joint List - were projected to win several extra seats in parliament following a reportedly strong turnout among Arab Israelis, who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.

They are emerging as the kingmakers in the election, but only one party has openly backed working with them in government.

"I hope that the numbers will work out and we, the Change Bloc and the UAL, can ensure that there are 61 Knesset seats," United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas said.

After the 2021 elections, Abbas's party was part of a governing coalition led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, which lasted a year before collapsing.

The chairman of the Joint List, Yousef Jabareen, warned that the grouping "cannot be ignored under any political scenario".

Tuesday's election was the first since the deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023 and the wars that followed in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

It was also seen by Israelis as one of the most consequential in the country's history, because it could decide not just their leadership but whether the country continues on its current hard-line, religious-nationalist trajectory.

Key campaign issues included accountability for the security failures that led to the 7 October attacks, the conduct of regional wars, how to share the growing burden of military service, judicial reforms, and Israel's international standing.

Outside a polling station in an opposition stronghold in northern Tel Aviv, campaigners young and old were out in force, using every last moment to win that extra vote.

Zivit Abramson, 88, told the BBC that she had voted for Eisenkot because Netanyahu was "ruining this country". "He's all about himself, only about himself," she added.

Elsewhere, Claire Tugendhaft said she had voted for Netanyahu "because I think he's the best man in the country to lead the country towards the outside world".

The prime minister and his government allies urged their supporters to head to the polls with warnings about a surge in turnout among left-wing and Arab voters.

"If you don't vote, we'll wake up tomorrow with a left-wing government, Arab parties, extreme Islam, and we'll lose the country," Netanyahu was filmed saying.

Likud and several other right-wing parties asked for voting hours to be extended beyond 22:00 local time - a move many of their opponents saw as a sign of growing desperation.

The Central Elections Committee ultimately rejected their request, saying that "the current circumstances do not justify an extension" and that the high turnout "reflects strong public engagement in the democratic process".

articles.title: Neil Young sues Trump for playing Rockin' in the Free World at a rally without a licence
articles.summary: The Canadian-American musician sued Trump in 2020 over unauthorised use of song at a political event.
articles.body:
Rock veteran Neil Young has filed a $10m lawsuit against a fundraising committee that supports US President Donald Trump, citing "unauthorised" use of his 1989 song Rockin' in the Free World.

The Canadian-American star alleges that the Trump 47 Committee infringed on his copyright when it played the song before Trump took the stage at a 12 October rally in Ohio. Playing the song amounts to an "unauthorised public performance", the lawsuit says.

The singer-songwriter sued the Trump re-election campaign in 2020 over its use of the same song and Devil's Sidewalk. Young said the parties settled the matter shortly thereafter.

The White House referred to the Republican National Committee, who the BBC has contacted for comment.

Through his company Silver Fiddle Music, Young alleges that the song was played without a licence or Young's permission at a political event in Youngstown, Ohio on 12 October.

In the US, music used at campaign rallies often requires a public performance licence for it to be played for an audience, even if a campaign has already purchased a legal copy of the recording.

According to US Congress, because sound recordings do not have a general public-performance right, permission is only needed from the musical-work copyright holders, which can be obtained directly from the copyright holders themselves or through performing rights organisations.

The five-page federal lawsuit says that Trump "was personally aware that a licence would be required to play the Song at rallies," and that Young "has not, and would not, grant the required licence". It also says the song has been played "numerous times at other rallies".

The Grammy Award winner, 80, who has strongly opposed Trump's politics, characterises the song as "a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless and forgotten".

Young says that the song is "the opposite of everything that Donald J Trump stands for".

In 2020, Young sued Trump's re-election campaign for copyright infringement over the same song, as well as Devil's Sidewalk.

The new lawsuit claims that the campaign, at the time, "asserted no defence and immediately settled shortly after it was served", promising to never use the song without permission again.

Young posted about the lawsuit on his website on Tuesday, thanking Trump for coming to so many of his shows in the 1980s and 1990s, but stopped short of allowing him to play his music.

"I am sorry it came to this, but money and transactions are something you understand," he wrote.

Young, The Rolling Stones, Rihanna, Adele, REM and the estate of Prince have previously criticised the president for using their music at campaign events.

articles.title: Five key takeaways from Israel’s parliamentary elections
articles.summary: With more than half of votes counted, Netanyahu’s bloc holds slight lead over opposition, but shy of majority.
articles.body:
Israel’s partial election results show a neck-and-neck race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, with neither likely to secure a clear path to a governing majority.

As per the partial results published by the Central Elections Committee, with 55 percent of the votes counted as of Wednesday morning, Netanyahu’s bloc stands at 56 Knesset seats and Eisenkot’s alliance is at 49.

Tuesday’s vote was largely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership and a response to the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, as well as Israel’s subsequent genocidal war on Gaza.

It also came as Israel’s pogroms in the occupied West Bank have escalated, and amid mounting tensions with several of the country’s neighbours, many of whom it has attacked in the past three years.

Here are five key takeaways from the Israeli elections so far:

Late-night exit polls from Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster projected the Netanyahu bloc would win 52 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, or Israeli parliament. In preliminary early results and exit polls, Netanyahu was edging out the opposition bloc led by former Israeli military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party, which was projected to win 49 seats.

Israel’s Channel 13 earlier indicated that Likud and the opposition were tied, with each winning 51 seats.

Polling indicated that Netanyahu’s Likud party – which leads his wider bloc – could emerge as the single largest party with an estimated 27 seats to 21 for Eisenkot’s Yashar party, according to updated projections from Channels 12 and 13 – giving Likud a clear lead over all others in the parliament.

Arab parties were projected to win 19 seats collectively, building on their 2022 performance.

Israelis vote for parties, which then form alliances to create a governing coalition with a prime minister at the helm. No single party has ever won a 61-seat majority.

Released by the major Israeli television networks, exit polls are unofficial indicators of the vote. Preliminary official results are expected on Wednesday, and may vary from the exit polls.

Leaders react, predict end to Netanyahu’s reign

Opposition bloc leader Eisenkot said the Israeli public had voted for change and against the incumbent prime minister.

Addressing supporters at his Yashar party headquarters, Eisenkot said, “This will be a new start. A real new start on a new path. The old era is over, and Israel is starting a new era.”

But the prime minister told supporters that his Likud party is dominant and called for the formation of a “national right-wing government”.

“What we’ve seen is that the Likud party is the largest party – nobody can compete with us,” he said. “The second thing that is clear as well is that the right bloc has a majority. And it is a decisive majority.”

He also accused Israeli television channels of trying to discourage his supporters from voting by projecting stronger results for opposition parties.

Far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich told supporters his party was projected to win seven seats, and pledged to continue the expansion of Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir praised his Otzma Yehudit party’s performance in a speech to supporters at its headquarters.

“We are very proud of our journey”, Ben-Gvir said. “This party was not even existing on the political landscape.”

The Democrats party leader Yair Golan said on X that voters had “fired the Netanyahu government”, and pledged to work with political partners to form a new administration.

The leader of Ra’am, or the United Arab List, Mansour Abbas said he hopes the final election results will let the opposition bloc and his party hold the 61 seats needed to form a government. The party was projected to win about seven seats.

The Central Elections Committee reported that 77.7 percent of eligible voters participated in the election, the highest turnout since 1999. Turnout was up 7.1 percentage points from 2022, when Netanyahu, who has served as prime minister off and on since 1996, returned to office .

Israel’s military said turnout among soldiers had climbed beyond 68 percent by 5pm local time (15:00 GMT). More than 60,000 Israelis also returned home from abroad to take part in the vote.

Polling stations closed at 10pm local time (20:00 GMT), but the official elections body said anyone waiting in line at that time would be allowed to vote.

Exit polls suggested Arab-led parties could win 19 seats , a significant jump from the current 10-seat representation they hold in parliament. That same polling showed Eisenkot and Netanyahu tied at the projected 51 seats each before preliminary official results began trickling in.

Given the 61 seats needed to form a government in Israel, both Eisenkot and Netanyahu’s parties are locked out of the majority without the Arab vote.

Eisenkot and Netanyahu have in the past refused to form a coalition with Arab parties to secure that majority. Netanyahu said the idea of working with Arab leaders would be a “ disgrace and a shame “.

Alon Pinkas, a former Israeli ambassador, told Al Jazeera that forming a government could be difficult for both parties because of the promise not to form said coalition.

“There’s a price to pay,” Pinkas said, because the “Arabs can’t be kept outside and only being considered and co-opted when you need their votes”.

After the vote is finalised, the parties will immediately begin negotiations to try to reach the 61-seat majority.

The bloc with the most votes will have different options to assemble support from smaller parties, including forming a minority government or working with another political leader to alternate as prime minister under a power-sharing arrangement.

Once the final count is in, President Isaac Herzog will speak with party leaders about who they want as prime minister. He will then tap the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government.

The person nominated will then have up to 42 days to form a government.

As for the two leading parties unifying to create a majority, voters would “never forgive” Eisenkot if he unites with Netanyahu’s bloc, while sharing power through rotating roles would guarantee “dysfunction”, Pinkas said.

If no government emerges, Netanyahu and his current cabinet will remain as a caretaker government.

If negotiations fail and no coalition can form a government, new elections will be called.

The final vote tally is expected by Friday, and official election results are formally published a week after the election, on November 4.

articles.title: Mahmoud Khalil credits Palestinian activism for reshaping US politics
articles.summary: Khalil returned to Columbia University to discuss his memoir detailing his arrest and detention by US immigration agents
articles.body:
Pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil says campus advocacy has shifted public perception and encouraged a generation of leaders to question their views on Israel, speaking as he returned to Columbia University for the first time since his arrest.

The 31-year-old Columbia graduate, who became a figurehead of the campus movement that swept the United States in 2024, returned to campus on Tuesday to discuss his new memoir, No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention , marking his first visit since his arrest on March 8, 2025.

“The American public is finally changing, is finally looking at the Palestinian as an equal human,” he told the AFP news agency in an interview.

While Khalil described the event, attended by about 100 people, as a “victory”, he accused university leadership of seeking “to erase me, to erase any Palestinian voices on campus”.

Some Jewish groups on social media opposed his return to campus. In response, a Columbia spokesperson said the university is “committed to rigorous debate, inquiry, and respectful dialogue across differing perspectives”.

“Columbia supports the right of faculty members to organize academic events,” the statement carried by US media read. “An invitation to speak does not signify university endorsement of a speaker’s views.”

Khalil helped lead student demonstrations at Columbia in 2024, which became the epicentre of nationwide campus protests against Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza. He was later arrested by immigration authorities at the height of a federal crackdown on foreign student activists and held for three months without criminal charge, despite holding permanent US residency.

He has repeatedly slammed the university for its handling of the demonstrations , which included authorising the New York Police Department to clear protesters from the Manhattan campus.

“They chose brutality. They chose repression,” Khalil told AFP.

Columbia maintained at the time that the demonstrations presented a safety threat. Khalil also accused the university of failing to protect him from harassment prior to his detention.

Despite the personal toll, Khalil credited Palestinian student advocacy with driving broader political shifts in the United States, pointing to gains by progressive candidates.

“Also, we can see on the ground that we have more progressive candidates being elected into US Congress and positions of power,” he said, citing candidates like Dr Abdul El-Sayed, running for the US Senate in Michigan, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Khalil was released from immigration custody on June 20, 2025, though the Trump administration continues to seek his deportation .

“A big part of my fight is like fighting for normalcy,” he said. “To go back to being the young father who would go to the park with his son and wife, and no one would bother them.”

Despite the ongoing legal battle, he expressed resolve over his public role.

“My fight is not only about whether I get to stay in this country,” Khalil said. “It is about whether, you know, people in this country can speak their minds.”

articles.title: 'This is America! Not your communist dictatorship': US, Cuban envoys scream at each other at UN - watch
articles.summary: A heated exchange broke out at the United Nations General Assembly after US Ambassador Mike Waltz told Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla to
articles.body: A heated exchange broke out at the United Nations General Assembly after US Ambassador Mike Waltz told Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla to “back up” when the Cuban diplomat approached the podium while Waltz was speaking.The confrontation took place during the General Assembly’s annual debate on the decades-old US embargo on Cuba, ahead of a vote on a resolution calling for an end to the restrictions.“Do you understand who you're dealing with? This is America!” Waltz said during the exchange, accusing the Cuban government of enriching its leaders while its people faced hardship.As the Cuban delegation sought to interrupt his remarks, Waltz said, “I know you don't like to hear this,” before adding, “This is America, my friend. This is the United Nations. This isn't your communist dictatorship. You cannot silence me.”Rodríguez continued towards the podium as the president of the General Assembly attempted to restore order, reminding delegates that the Cuban delegation would have an opportunity to respond.“This individual needs to back away from this podium,” Waltz said. “He's not going to intimidate me in the United States of America.”“I'm the representative of the United States of America. Back up! Back up, Ambassador. Back away! This isn't Havana.”Waltz urged UN member states to reject the resolution seeking to end the US embargo. He blamed corruption and repression within Cuba for the hardships faced by its people and accused the country’s communist government of enriching itself.After Cuba was given the floor, Rodríguez accused Waltz of making false claims and asked the General Assembly president to call him to order.“Mr. Waltz is lying yet again,” he said, arguing that the US ambassador’s remarks were “beneath the dignity of this forum and member states” and were insulting to Cuba’s government and people.In a subsequent post on X, Waltz accused Cuba’s “Communist leaders” of concealing their luxury real estate holdings, adding that he was presenting evidence that the delegation did not want discussed.The confrontation came amid renewed debate over Washington’s decades-old economic embargo on Cuba, which has remained a point of contention between the two countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: An alleged $65 million scam targeting elderly Americans used India-based call centres and fake rental addresses to collect cash; US prosecutors say YouTube scam hunters helped identify suspects as guilty pleas emerged
articles.summary: A multinational fraud scheme that allegedly cost elderly Americans about $65 million relied on India-based scam call centres, fake identities and
articles.body: A multinational fraud scheme that allegedly cost elderly Americans about $65 million relied on India-based scam call centres, fake identities and short-term rental properties to collect cash from victims, according to the US Department of Justice (DOJ). In an update published on October 26, prosecutors said the final defendants among 25 people arrested in the case had pleaded guilty, marking a significant development in an investigation that was also aided by YouTube creators who confronted suspected scammers on camera and shared footage with law enforcement.The criminal network, which prosecutors said had operated since at least 2019 and was rooted in Southern California, targeted thousands of older Americans through elaborate refund and technical-support scams. The operation primarily involved Chinese nationals who allegedly worked with India-based call centres, according to court records. Three charged defendants remained fugitives as of the latest DOJ announcement.The investigation also highlighted how videos made by online scam hunters helped authorities identify people linked to the alleged conspiracy and understand how the network collected money from victims across the United States.How the scam allegedly workedAccording to prosecutors, victims received unsolicited calls or emails that directed them to phone numbers connected to scam call centres in India. People answering the calls posed as technical-support agents, government officials or bank employees.Using scripted claims and psychological manipulation, they allegedly persuaded victims that they had received a mistaken refund or faced a problem requiring immediate action. In some cases, scammers obtained remote access to victims’ computers. They then pressured or threatened victims into returning supposed excess payments through wire transfers, cash or gift cards.For victims instructed to send cash, the process was particularly elaborate. They were told to withdraw large sums, place the money in packages and send them through express or overnight delivery services to addresses supplied by the conspirators.The recipient names were fictitious and corresponded with fake identification documents, while the addresses belonged to short-term rental properties in the US, prosecutors said. The arrangements allowed members of the network to receive cash without consistently using their real names or permanent addresses.According to the DOJ, conspirators booked properties using a hub-and-spoke pattern. A central property would be rented for about a week, while nearby locations were booked for shorter periods. The group would then move to different properties and repeat the process, making it harder for investigators to trace the operation.A package of cash led investigators to the networkThe investigation began in December 2020 after an elderly victim contacted an express-mail carrier after being defrauded into sending cash through the post. The discovery led investigators to 11 packages containing approximately $135,000, all addressed to fictitious names at short-term rental properties in the San Diego area. Authorities subsequently uncovered a much larger alleged operation involving thousands of victims and millions of dollars in losses.One of the victims identified in the case was a 97-year-old San Diego widow whose entire life savings were allegedly taken. The case prompted federal investigators to pursue the people collecting the cash as well as those involved in the calls and financial transactions.In August 2025, federal agents carried out a coordinated nationwide operation, making arrests in California, New York, Texas and Michigan. The DOJ announced charges against 28 alleged members of the network, with 25 arrested during the operation. The government said the investigation involved the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations and the Internal Revenue Service's Criminal Investigation division, among other agencies.How YouTube scam hunters helpedThe case also drew attention to the role played by online creators who specialise in exposing scams. Prosecutors credited YouTubers from Scammer Payback, whose creator is known as Pierogi, and Trilogy Media with helping investigators identify multiple defendants.In videos published in 2020 and 2021, the creators staged sting operations designed to expose suspected scammers. They posed as victims, followed instructions to send decoy packages and confronted people who appeared to be involved in collecting money.In one operation described by the DOJ, a suspected recipient was directed to collect a cash package under the alias “Hans Bum”. Trilogy Media delivered a decoy package to a South San Francisco address and confronted the recipient, identified by prosecutors as Zhiyi Zhang. According to the government, Zhang revealed his identity during the interaction and acknowledged receiving packages for money.The creators handed footage to law enforcement. Investigators then used unblurred video, rental records and other evidence to verify identities and establish links to the alleged operation.Prosecutors said the videos helped identify Zhiyi Zhang, Dudu Chen and Huajian Chen, while also providing insight into how the wider conspiracy operated. The footage was one part of a broader investigation that relied on financial records, surveillance, interviews and evidence gathered by federal agencies.The latest DOJ announcement said Haotian Zhang and Zetian Zhang pleaded guilty in federal court on October 23, with the announcement issued three days later. Other defendants had also entered guilty pleas in preceding months, including Hua Wang, whom prosecutors identified as a lead defendant.In a June 2026 announcement, the DOJ said Wang admitted participating in the scheme from 2019 through 2023 and being responsible for more than 2,000 cash packages sent by elderly victims. Prosecutors attributed approximately $64 million in victim losses to his role.The October update said three charged defendants remained fugitives. Sentencing proceedings for multiple defendants were still pending, meaning guilty pleas did not mark the end of the legal process.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Can a murder conviction be set aside if an accused is questioned in a language he doesn’t understand? Jharkhand HC explains
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Can a murder conviction be upheld if an accused was not properly questioned about the evidence against him during the trial?
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Can a murder conviction be upheld if an accused was not properly questioned about the evidence against him during the trial? The Jharkhand high court has ruled that an accused must get a fair opportunity to explain the circumstances used against him, setting aside a man's murder conviction after finding serious lapses in how his statement was recorded.In its October 1, 2026, judgment, the high court acquitted a man who had been sentenced to life imprisonment for allegedly drowning a woman in a well. The court found that the illiterate accused had been questioned in English without any record showing that the questions and answers were translated and explained to him in a language he understood.Why did the man challenge his murder conviction?As per the court order, the case arose from an incident on February 26, 2009, when the accused allegedly jumped into a well while holding a woman and pushed her underwater. The woman's husband also jumped into the well but survived after villagers helped him get out but the woman died.The prosecution alleged that the incident was planned because of a land dispute. Police registered a murder case and filed a chargesheet under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, which deals with murder.In April 2018, a sessions court convicted the accused and sentenced him to life imprisonment, along with a fine of Rs 20,000. He challenged the conviction before the high court.His counsel argued that the prosecution's statements contained contradictions and the deceased's body had no injuries. The state maintained that eyewitness accounts and medical evidence supported the prosecution's case.Why did the high court find the trial unfair?The division bench of Justice Ananda Sen and Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava examined how the trial court recorded the accused's statement under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).This provision requires the court to give an accused an opportunity to explain circumstances in the prosecution's evidence that may be used against him. The questioning is an important safeguard in a criminal trial and not just a formality.The high court noted that the accused was an illiterate villager and that his thumb impression appeared on the statement. The questions and answers had been recorded in English, but the record did not show that they had been translated into his mother tongue or explained to him in that language.“This is a serious lapse in the trial, and it goes to the root of the matter and shakes the edifice of a fair trial in this case,” the court said.The court also questioned an endorsement showing that the statement was recorded on July 22, 2016, but the printout and the accused's thumb impression were obtained the next day because of a power failure. It said the accused had not been made to understand the document's contents.“A person who doesn’t even know how to read, write, or understand English should not be asked any questions in that language,” the bench further added.The bench also examined the prosecution's evidence before deciding whether to send the case back to the trial court. It found contradictions in the informant's account of where he was standing when the accused allegedly caught the deceased. The informant also said the water in the well was three feet deep, raising questions about how the woman could have been forcibly drowned in those conditions.The medical evidence recorded no external or internal mechanical injuries on the woman's body, despite witnesses claiming she had been injured. The court also noted that the investigating officer denied visiting the spot and the officer who recorded witness statements was not examined.The bench concluded that these gaps, combined with the failure to properly question the accused, undermined the prosecution's case.It held that the prosecution had failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt. The high court allowed the appeal, set aside the conviction and life sentence, and directed the man's release if he was not required in any other case.

articles.title: In New Jersey, painter John Fricano built Jack and Jill’s Hill and the Three Bears’ house for his kids in 1955; Storybook Land grew to 20 acres, with 19 rides
articles.summary: Discover Storybook Land in New Jersey, a magical park founded by John Fricano in 1955, perfect for young kids with rides, attractions, and nursery rhyme themes. Learn about its history, growth, and the importance of early childhood experiences.
articles.body: Storybook Land is a family-owned children’s amusement park in southern New Jersey, on a highway that was once the main route for families heading to the shore. The park is built around fairy tales and nursery rhymes, with small cottages, storybook characters, shaded paths and rides sized for young children. Unlike the large theme parks built around big rides, it was designed for very young visitors. It began as the project of a local house painter, who built its first attractions himself and it is still run by his family across several generations.Five wooded acres in Egg Harbor Township and a founding in 1955John Fricano, an Army veteran and house painter and his wife Esther established Storybook Land on a five-acre wooded lot in Egg Harbor Township, New Jersey and the park’s website dates its founding to 1955. The Philadelphia Inquirer places the opening in July of that year and reports that admission was 75 cents, with two simple rides for visitors. Some of the attractions Fricano built himself include Little Red Schoolhouse, Old Woman’s Shoe and Jack and Jill’s Hill. NJ Monthly also lists the Three Bears House among the attractions. In a 2015 interview with The Philadelphia Inquirer, their granddaughter Jessica Fricano said her grandparents saw that there was little for children to do and that the park began as a luncheonette.From 20 acres and 14 rides in 2015 to 19 rides on the park’s website todayThe park later grew from its original five acres to 20 acres, WPG Talk Radio reported. Fricano died in 2009, Roadtrippers notes. By 2015, the park had 14 rides, including Bubbles the Coaster and a miniature train ride called the J&J Railroad, the Inquirer reported. The park’s website now lists 19 rides, including the Cinderoller Coaster, a pumpkin-coach ride introduced for the 2025 season.The same 2015 Inquirer report said Jessica Fricano was running the park with her father, John Fricano Jr., her brother and her aunt. A long-time staff member told NJ Monthly the park is designed for children between ages 1 and 8.The Little Red Schoolhouse as the last original structure and a new attraction each yearLittle of the park’s original construction remains, but its approach has stayed largely the same. In an earlier feature, Roadtrippers reported that the Little Red Schoolhouse is the only original structure still standing and that the family adds at least one new attraction a year while occasionally feeling pressure to chase the latest ride. Among the additions it described was a Robin Hood statue brought from a park in New York and restored for Storybook Land. The park’s website says it operates from spring through December, with ticketed events at Halloween and Christmas toward the end of the year.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
